Subject: MAP: smokeproof decision-lattice + ops evidence for Mediq trial signoff

Hi Elena —

Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan for the 6-week Mediq pilot. I've framed the MAP around three pillars so we can be explicit when we talk about "done":

1) Business success (outcome metrics) — conversion uplift on triage flows, end-user throughput, and false-alert reduction targets.
2) Technical exit gates — smoke tests (functional), perf sanity (p50/p95 tokens and latency under 250ms for core routes), and data residency verification.
3) Operational evidence — what we need from Mediq and what Redwood will deliver (observability traces, per-route token cost reports, and runbook checks).

Key ask: review the acceptance tests section (tab 3 in the spreadsheet) and flag any additional evidence you need for internal signoff (security, legal, or IT). I called out owners and signoff criteria for each gate. If this structure looks good, we can lock timelines and generate a short signoff agenda for next week's working session.

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx (MAP with timeline + owners) and an observability spec stub that lists trace/log examples we will hand to Mediq for their verification.

Proposed milestone highlights:
- Week 1 (Mar 15): integration + smoke-run (ok to proceed if core flows pass)
- Week 3 (Mar 29): perf ramp + telemetry verification (Redwood to deliver token-cost dashboard)
- Week 5 (Apr 12): evidence collection complete; stakeholder review
- Week 6 (Apr 19): signoff / handshake or rollback decision

If helpful I can convert the MAP into a mutual checklist (DocuSign link) for each owner.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Camila —

Thanks for the clear structure. A couple of quick clarifications from our side before we run the working session:

- Observability: when you say "per-route token cost reports" can you confirm cadence and whether we'll be able to slice by environment (staging vs prod)? We need daily rolling windows for finance to model committed spend.
- Latency SLA: our threshold for the front-end is p95 < 300ms end-to-end. I see you've called 250ms for core routes — can you explain whether that is server-only or includes network + client processing?
- Data residency & logs: our security team will need proof of where model inputs are stored (ephemeral vs persisted) and a sample of audit log format for a request. Is that in the observability stub?

Also Andre asked whether an abbreviated acceptance test matrix (pass/fail with owner initials) is possible — he's trying to map it to our vendor review checklist.

If you can update the MAP with those three clarifications (per-route cost cadence, latency definition, and audit-log sample) that should unblock our internal review. Happy to review a new version before the call.

Best,
Elena Morris
Head of Product Operations | Mediq Health
elena.morris@mediq.com
